sonnet.detail: The stock versus flow distinction (a common basic concept, e.g. wealth as a stock, income as a flow) has no subtopic under national-income or basics. Q28 tests it directly and has to be forced onto national-income.concepts.

The Phillips curve, linking inflation and unemployment, is not named under inflation or labour. Q40 tests it directly with no natural home; it sits across two parents (inflation and labour.unemployment).
Open versus closed economy is a standard classification distinct from capitalism, socialism and mixed economy, but systems.types only covers the latter three. Q51 tests it and has no subtopic.
A single-stem question can ask for the price relationship in both demand and supply at once (Q7). Each subtopic covers only its own law, so a combined question has no single home.

The covers lines split the monetary policy instrument from how it controls inflation, but a question naming a policy stance (contractionary vs expansionary) and its inflation purpose in one stem (Q39) sits on both sides at once.
Neither subtopic's covers line addresses what limits government's ability to collect tax (e.g. political instability), so a question on obstacles to tax revenue (Q38) could go to either.

business.finance covers a firm's sources of funds but explicitly routes how the stock exchange works to financial.markets. A question asking which institution a firm approaches to raise funds, where the answer is the stock exchange (Q59), sits exactly on that line.

opus.detail: No place for basic analytical concepts such as stock and flow variables, economic variables and functions (Q28). Add a subtopic under tools or widen tools.methods.
Phillips curve and the inflation-unemployment trade-off have no home (Q40). Add to inflation.effects-control covers or a new subtopic.
Open versus closed economy is nowhere (Q51). Add to trade.basis covers or national-income.circular-flow.
demand.law and supply.law split a question that asks both laws at once (Q7), and neither covers evaluating a demand or supply function outside equilibrium (Q54), which drifts to price.equilibrium.
Per capita income as a living-standard measure sits in both national-income.uses and development.meaning with no sorting rule (Q30).

inflation.effects-control claims monetary measures to control inflation and financial.monetary-policy claims instruments and their effects; a question on what contractionary monetary policy is for fits both (Q39).
The price mechanism is claimed by price.market-system, systems.economic-problems and, via system features, systems.types (Q46, Q50, Q52). Needs one sorting rule.
Challenges facing banks in Nigeria are only in financial.types, which sends commercial banks away to financial.deposit-banks, whose covers line has no challenges (Q34).
Migration sits in population.size-growth while geographical distribution sits in population.structure; a question on why people move to an area straddles both (Q9).
Mono-product (single export) economies fit development.problems and trade.structure equally; neither names the concept (Q75).
Covers contributions, linkages, NNPC and OPEC but not problems of the oil and gas industry, a common question type (Q47).
Covers line lists UNCTAD, ECA, WTO, OECD, AU, EU but not UN specialised agencies such as WHO (Q21); the scope rule should say where general UN questions go.
Scope rule lists off-syllabus current-affairs items but not power sector unbundling of NEPA/PHCN (Q53); it fits here only by inference.
